summary: Customer C00348 reported unauthorized activity on card C00348-K1 regarding online transaction 3660250 ($4.05, product C). An investigation identified a sequence of six online micro-authorizations in product category C between January 7 and January 28, 2017, totaling $23.17, which completely departed from the cardholder's baseline of in-person retail spending. Graph analysis linked the activity to an automated micro-billing scheme spanning 19 additional customer cards with sequential transaction IDs between 3660174 and 3660349. Based on decisive evidence of coordinated cross-customer abuse fitting undocumented pattern R9, card C00348-K1 was blocked, connected cards were placed on monitoring, and a regulatory report was authorized.
open_question: While the cross-customer scheme of sequential micro-authorizations under $10 is evident from graph peers and consecutive transaction numbering, the specific merchant identifier or payment processor channel facilitating these charges without device fingerprints remains unknown. Accessing merchant descriptor names or processor terminals for the 3660174-3660349 series would identify the compromise point.
